entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Casts the same unpermitted advance as an incursion, force rather than the patient creep of *encroaching*.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Makes the offensive prying a settled trait of the person, not the single act that *meddling* catches them at.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Condemns the deed in progress, where *meddlesome* condemns the character behind it.

entries.definition: intrusive in a meddling or offensive manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and cold beside the homely *busybodied*, delivering the same charge of offensive meddling as a verdict rather than a complaint.
examples: bustling about self-importantly making an officious nuisance of himself

entries.definition: gradually intrusive without right or permission
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the intrusion in terms of a line crossed without permission, naming the wrong outright where *encroaching* only lets it accumulate.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Measures the overshoot rather than judging it: a quantity past the mark, not a fault.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The easiest word here to hear without complaint - what lies beyond the requirement can simply be available, where *superfluous* would call the same amount waste.
examples: found some extra change lying on the dresser
extra ribs as well as other supernumerary internal parts

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The harshest of these - not merely that the thing was not needed, but that nothing justified it at all.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The gentlest here - it grants that the thing may well be wanted and withholds only the claim that it is strictly required.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sounds the note of waste - unwarranted, and the sting is that it happened anyway; softer in rebuke than *gratuitous*.
examples: a strikers' tent camp … was burned with needless loss of life

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sharper than *excess* - the surplus is treated as serving no purpose, not merely as a quantity over the line.
examples: yet another book on heraldry might be thought redundant
skills made redundant by technological advance

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Frames what is past the requirement as held in reserve, so it reads as usable rather than as clutter.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and weighty, marking the amount as going beyond what was required at all, with a dryness *extra* does not have.
examples: it was supererogatory of her to gloat

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Dismissive where *excess* stays quantitative: it says the thing could be stripped away and nothing would be lost.

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Positional and countable - it sets something outside the number required without passing any verdict on it.
examples: extra ribs as well as other supernumerary internal parts

entries.definition: more than is needed, desired, or required
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A ledger word: it registers the amount left over as a balance and carries no complaint about it.
examples: surplus cheese distributed to the needy

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A rebuke rather than an assessment: it says the thing overstepped, where *unnecessary* only says it was not required.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The family's plain verdict - it states the thing was not needed and leaves any reproach implied rather than spoken, where *gratuitous* speaks it.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Flatter than *unnecessary* - it reports an absence of need without the faint blame that clings to the other word.

entries.definition: (of a record) having no marks of discredit or offense
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise by absence - a record with nothing marked against it, a narrower claim than the completeness *perfect* asserts.

entries.definition: free from flaw or blemish or impurity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Reaches past flaw and blemish to impurity as well, so it can clear a substance and not only a performance.
examples: the clear complexion of a healthy young woman

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Perfection as drilled familiarity - the thing is known so thoroughly that error does not arise, where *errorless* only reports that none did.
examples: had her lines cold before rehearsals started

entries.definition: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Asserts that every necessary quality is present, the opposite test from *flawless*: nothing missing rather than nothing wrong.

entries.definition: perfect and complete in every respect; having all necessary qualities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Formal and superlative where *complete* is plain, pitching the same total sufficiency as an accolade.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Puts the perfection in the grasp rather than in the thing - the understanding is finished, and it says so flatly.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The idiom tightens *down* into exactness: not merely understood but understood to the letter.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A flat count of no errors, the coolest word in the family beside *impeccable*'s admiration.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Takes in fault as well as error, so it acquits the conduct and not just the execution.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Single-minded - one flaw would undo it, where *complete* asks instead whether everything is there.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Lifts the same absence of fault into something untouched, admiring where *errorless* is merely accurate.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Reads the absence of fault as a standard held to - admiration rather than measurement.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Frames faultlessness as something kept intact rather than achieved, and in a stiffer register than *faultless*.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dignifies the same perfect understanding as an attainment, where *down* merely reports the state.

entries.definition: being complete of its kind and without defect or blemish
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unqualified standard here, claiming completeness of its kind as well as the absence of blemish, where *flawless* claims only the absence.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plain negation beside *flawless*, denying the flaw without carrying the admiration.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unheated name for the state: impatience or anger without the colouring that *miffed* or *steamed* add to it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Flat, worn British informality, the patience gone by erosion rather than blown out like *steamed*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and deflating: a full loss of patience carried in a phrase too offhand to shout, where *exasperated* keeps its composure.

entries.definition: having a strong distaste from surfeit
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Strong distaste from having had too much of a thing, the surfeited turn of the stomach rather than heat aimed at anyone, and the family's furthest recoil.

entries.definition: not pleased; experiencing or manifesting displeasure
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The family's coolest term: it registers the absence of pleasure and lets it show, without conceding any heat to it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The end of the line, annoyance carried far enough that patience is spent, which is exactly what *annoyed* still holds in reserve.
examples: had an exasperated look on his face

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Friction rather than flare: the same impatience or anger, but felt as something rubbing on and on rather than landing once like *stung*.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Light and slightly diminishing, it sizes the impatience or anger as a small thing and the person holding it as easily put out, where *annoyed* passes no such judgement.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Prickled and smarting: the state as something that caught and stings still, sharper in point than *annoyed* and briefer than *irritated*.
examples: feeling nettled from the constant teasing

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Small and faintly comic, it scales the impatience or anger down to a grievance worth mentioning but not worth raising your voice over.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Vulgar and blunt, it states the same impatience or anger in the coarsest register the family has, which is everything *displeased* withholds.
examples: felt really pissed at her snootiness

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the coarse charge of *pissed* with the particle adding follow-through, anger sent outward rather than merely held.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stirred up rather than simply arrived at: it puts the impatience or anger down to having been worked into someone.
examples: riled no end by his lies
